narrative.overview: Nora Intelligence System presents as a precise, technical document. The visual language relies on a cool white backdrop, deep navy serif headlines, and deliberate teal pill-shaped actions. It prioritizes clarity over flourish, utilizing framed canonical diagrams and cool-toned cards to make engineering boundaries easy to examine. The density is relaxed but structured. Information is chunked into bordered containers that establish a clear architectural rhythm. The Founders section inherits this system cleanly, presenting data-driven profiles that currently feature Michael Lvov alone, with structural readiness for Alla to be added later.
keyCharacteristics: Navy serif headlines (Libre Caslon Display) with muted blue emphasis.
Structured, bordered containers for architectural chunking.

rules.name: The Cool Ground Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds must remain strictly cool and near-white. Avoid warm grays or off-whites; the system's clarity depends on the cool atlas aesthetic.

rules.name: The Serif Leadership Rule
rules.body: Serif fonts are reserved for headings. Body text, UI controls, and labels use Public Sans to maintain technical readability.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows or drop-shadows appear only as a response to interactive state (hover, active, focus).

dos: Do use the full name "Nora Intelligence System" or "NIS".
Do use bordered containers (1px solid Divider Frost) to separate architectural concepts.
Do maintain the data-driven structure for the Founders section so Michael Lvov and Alla can be rendered dynamically.
Do use `mailto:` links for contact authorizations.
donts: Don't include credentials, private model routes, or live chat UI in the project documentation or interfaces.
Don't use warm grays or off-whites; stick to the cool atlas palette (Atlas Cool, Paper White).
Don't apply shadows to resting elements; reserve them for active states (The Flat-By-Default Rule).
Don't replace serif headings with sans-serif fonts (The Serif Leadership Rule).
